purpose: Cross-system curriculum placement for Grade 1-6 statistics and probability concepts.

verification_policy.CN: Use the 2022 MOE mathematics standard at learning-stage level. Detailed content is partially verified through accessible transcriptions where direct page extraction is unavailable. Exact current PEP grade/semester remains separate.
verification_policy.UK: Use the statutory National Curriculum in England. Probability is not statutory Key Stage 1 or 2 content; the statutory probability strand begins at Key Stage 3.
verification_policy.US: Use Common Core as the comparison baseline. Chance/probability standards begin in Grade 7, so Grade 1-6 should not be given invented probability placements.

stages.expectation: Classify objects/data and record classification results using simple forms such as words, pictures or tables.
Experience simple processes of collecting, organising, describing and analysing data.
Collect, organise and analyse data according to the needs of a practical question and state conclusions.

placement.expectation: Construct simple statistical representations and ask/answer questions about categorical data; programme guidance also refers to recording, collating and organising information.
Present and interpret data in tables, pictograms and bar charts.

UK.notes: The statutory statements focus more on representation and interpretation than on a separately named data-collection objective.

placement.expectation: Organise, represent and interpret categorical data.
Generate measurement data through measuring objects or repeated measurement.
Generate measurement data using rulers.
Formulate statistical questions and understand data sets collected to answer them.

stages.expectation: Classify data by a chosen/given criterion and record results.
Organise and present collected data and analyse simple information.
Organise and represent data using appropriate statistical displays.

placement.expectation: Interpret and construct pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams and tables; collate and organise information.
Present data using bar charts, pictograms and tables.
Present discrete and continuous data using appropriate graphical methods.
Organise and represent data with up to three categories.
Represent categorical data with picture and bar graphs.
Display and summarize numerical data distributions.

stages.expectation: Tables may be used to record and describe classification results.
Use simple statistical tables/representations to present organised data.
Read statistical tables from practical/media contexts as part of data analysis.

placement.expectation: Interpret and construct simple tables.
Interpret and present data using tables.
Use tables as part of statistical interpretation.
Complete, read and interpret information in tables including timetables.
Tables may support statistical work, but Common Core Grade 6 formal display requirements specify number-line plots rather than a dedicated table standard.

US.notes: Do not equate general use of tables with an explicit Common Core table standard.

placement.expectation: Pictures may be used to record classification results, but the 2022 standard does not establish pictograms as a named formal statistical chart progression comparable with England.
Interpret and construct simple pictograms.
Interpret and present data using pictograms, including scaled representations.
Solve problems using information in pictograms and other graphs.
Draw picture graphs for categorical data.
Draw scaled picture graphs for categorical data.

stages.expectation: Recognise bar charts and use them appropriately to represent and analyse data.
Use bar charts as one available statistical representation and interpret their meaning.

placement.expectation: Interpret and present data using bar charts.
Present discrete/continuous data using methods including bar charts and solve comparison/sum/difference problems.
Draw single-unit-scale bar graphs and solve problems using them.
Draw scaled bar graphs and solve one- and two-step comparison problems.

CN.expectation: Recognise and use line graphs to present related data and explain what the graph shows.

placement.expectation: Present continuous data with appropriate graphical methods including time graphs.
Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using information in line graphs.
Interpret and construct line graphs and use them to solve problems.

US.notes: Common Core uses line plots/dot plots and coordinate graphs, but these should not be relabelled as the time-series line-graph concept used in England/China.

CN.expectation: Recognise fan/pie charts and interpret the part-whole information they communicate; the standard emphasises statistical meaning and appropriate representation.

placement.expectation: Interpret and construct pie charts and use them to solve problems.

CN.expectation: Explore the meaning of the mean, understand it as a statistic representing the central tendency of a data set, and solve simple practical problems with it.

placement.expectation: Calculate and interpret the mean as an average and know when it is appropriate to use it.
Understand measures of center and summarize numerical data with median and/or mean in context.

stages.expectation: Describe classification results and identify similarities/differences.
Analyse simple data, read statistical charts and use data to communicate information.
Analyse collected data, read statistical displays from media, explain meanings and state simple conclusions.

placement.expectation: Ask and answer questions about categorical data.
Solve one- and two-step questions from bar charts, pictograms and tables.
Solve comparison, sum and difference problems from graphical displays.
Read line graphs and tables.
Use pie charts/line graphs and mean to solve statistical problems.
Answer total/category/comparison questions from categorical data.
Solve problems using bar-graph data.
Solve comparison problems from scaled graphs.
Interpret numerical distributions and summarize them in context.

CN.expectation: Recognise simple random phenomena and use qualitative language to describe relative possibility in experiments/games.

UK.notes: The statutory probability strand begins at Key Stage 3.

US.notes: Common Core chance/probability standards begin in Grade 7.

CN.expectation: Understand occurrence/non-occurrence and relative likelihood of simple random phenomena qualitatively; primary 2022 content should not be presented as formal numerical probability calculation unless direct evidence supports it.
Use trials, games and simple experiments to experience randomness and compare qualitative likelihood; focus is on data awareness rather than formal long-run numerical probability theory.

UK.notes: Simple probability experiments enter the statutory programme at Key Stage 3.

US.notes: Experimental probability appears from Grade 7, including relative-frequency approximations.

cross_system_notes: China 2022 introduces qualitative chance/randomness in Grades 5-6, while England statutory primary mathematics and Common Core Grades 1-6 do not include a probability strand.

England explicitly introduces pie charts and the mean in Year 6. Common Core Grade 6 instead focuses on variability, distributions and measures of center such as mean/median, without a pie-chart requirement.
Do not treat Common Core line plots as equivalent to line graphs used to show change over time.
